issue_context.title: TCP2 does not send our MSS to peer
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
We do not send our MSS (maximum segment size) to peer. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maximum_segment_size

The default value 536 is used if not set. Usually we could advertise larger value in order to send data is bigger chunks.

review_comments:
Another concern is that reusing `struct tcp_options`, initially intended just for received options, also for send options, leads to a weird terminology, if using existing field names. IMHO, the fields should be renamed to more neutral first, e.g. `mss_found` -> `has_mss`.

(That's of course assuming the implementation approach taken in this PR is in the right direction.)

Isn't this just too magic/adhoc? MSS option happens to be 4 bytes, and that's why you use uint32_t here.

Wouldn't it be better to have a generic function which can add any TCP option to a header? IIRC, we used to have such in TCP1, sad if we lost it with switch to TCP2.

So, at best it looks like premature optimization (assuming it's actually more optimal to UNALIGNED_PUT a 32bit number instead of doing it byte by byte, which I'd doubt). And otherwise, it just obfuscated code with those `NET_TCP_MSS_OPT << 24`.
@pfalcon which "general" function are you talking about? This one?
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/ed2162c700e1a887f54c001d297b7523063f161e/subsys/net/ip/tcp.c#L727-L746
@finikorg 

> @pfalcon which "general" function are you talking about? This one?

Thanks for digging that out, yes, that's apparently what I meant, and memory about its "generality" apparently failed me ;-). So well, feel free to ignore this review comment, the new impl is on par with the old, and if someone will need to add arbitrary options later, it can be refactored later either.
